speaker_role: current admissions officer, Director of Undergraduate Admissions at Dartmouth College (20+ years at Dartmouth, over a decade as director)
commercial_incentive: Service to School is a nonprofit providing free admissions support to veterans; no sales pitch, public-service framing throughout
key_insights: Dartmouth defines any applicant who has enrolled in any college coursework as a 'transfer applicant,' but gives veterans flexibility to choose whichever admission round (early decision, regular decision, or transfer) fits their timeline
Dartmouth's transfer application was built in consultation with Service to School to give veterans essay prompts similar to that organization's supplement, even if they don't use it
Financial aid paperwork deadlines align with each admission round's application deadline (Nov 1 ED, Feb 1 RD, March 1 transfer), with aid offers arriving alongside the admission decision
For transfer applicants, Dartmouth doesn't finalize credit transfer evaluations until after matriculation, since faculty must review actual course syllabi first
Dartmouth has never required veterans to submit standardized testing, citing that in-military testing conditions and old high school scores are often unrepresentative

Admissions review is organized around four guiding questions: what the applicant cares most about, what choices they've made, their proudest (not necessarily formally recognized) successes, and how they impact others/community
Recommendation letters from military supervisors or online instructors are treated as fully valid alternatives to traditional academic teacher/advisor letters for veteran applicants

Submitting an application the day it opens does not improve chances; Dartmouth doesn't begin reviewing files until much closer to the round's deadline, and a full veteran candidacy file accumulates over months
specific_numbers_or_facts: Early decision deadline November 1 (notify mid-December); regular decision deadline January 2 (notify end of March, reply by May 1); transfer deadline March 1 (notify mid-May, 1-2 week reply window) (per Paul Sunde)
A full Common App is described as about eight pages of text; a complete candidacy file with essays and recommendations runs 30-40 pages (per Paul Sunde)
Dartmouth has enrolled veterans ranging from their early 20s to their 50s (per Paul Sunde)
notable_or_distinctive: A direct interview with a sitting Ivy League admissions director specifically addressing how policies (transfer definitions, testing requirements, recommendation letter sourcing, timeline flexibility) are adapted for military veteran and active-duty applicants.
reliability_notes: Reflects one officer's account of his own institution's current policies, subject to change; framing is candid and non-commercial given the nonprofit host; figures are not independently verified but are consistent with publicly known Dartmouth admissions norms.
